item.title: Memorials
item.content:encoded:
Martin Persson, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign

The Accounting Horizons Memorials Committee seeks nominations for memorials to be published in the journal, honoring deceased individuals who made significant contributions to accounting thought or practice. Nominees must have passed away at least 365 days before nomination.

Nominations should include a letter describing the nominee's contributions, three to five supporting letters, relevant primary source materials, and the nominee's vita or resume. All materials must be combined into a single PDF and submitted to memorials@aaahq.org.

Appel publié par Accounting Horizons. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Individuals whose work significantly advanced accounting thought
  • Individuals who revolutionized accounting practice and professional development

Timeline

  • November 30, 2026: Nomination submission deadline
  • March 1, 2027: Decisions will be announced

item.title: Broadening Research Methods to Bridge the Gap between Research and Practice
item.content:encoded:
Wayne Thomas, University of Oklahoma

Alessandro Ghio, ESCP

Accounting Horizons aims to bridge accounting academics and non-academics (e.g., practitioners, standard setters, and regulators) by publishing rigorous academic research and thought-provoking perspectives that are pertinent to the accounting profession. Most accounting research in the past few decades uses archival, experimental, or analytical methods, rather than other research methods, such as literature reviews, surveys, interviews, and field studies. Accounting Horizons recognizes that these other research methods have an important role to play in bridging the gap between academic research and accounting practice.

Literature review articles can inform academics about what knowledge has been discovered and where gaps exist. These articles can be particularly useful to non-academics who are interested in the given topic and seek insights from research. Literature review articles in Accounting Horizons should focus on specific topics relevant to practice and be written for both academics and non-academics who are interested in the topic, using plain language and avoiding jargon.

Appel publié par Accounting Horizons. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Literature review articles on topics relevant to accounting practice
  • Survey research on important accounting issues
  • Interview-based research gathering input from practitioners and non-academics
  • Field studies in accounting contexts
  • Qualitative research using positivist, interpretive, or critical paradigmatic lenses
  • Research methods beyond traditional archival, experimental, and analytical approaches

Timeline

  • December 31, 2026: Deadline for submitting research proposals. This is an open call that will continue accepting submissions until this date.
  • February 18, 2027: Deadline for submitting completed article following first-stage approval of research proposal.
